items.title: 56679_Arthur Briggs oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee confirms Gwendolyn Coleridge-Taylor was the pianist on a program featuring works by Coleridge-Taylor, but no personal interaction or relationship with the composer is described.

ctx.x: copy of the program, in front of me, and they were primarily the conversations with Coleridge-Taylor, and they were, "Symphonic Variations on an African Aire", a song, "Hiawatha's Vision," solos by W.A. Mikell, "Scenes from an Imaginary Ballet", "Concerto In G-Minor." The soloist was Winifred Small. "A Monologue; the Clown and Columbine," with violin-cello and piano accompaniment.
